# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 25 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 25 | **Condition:** very fragmentary

---

**1** [...] for [...] my heart [...] shook with terror at Your judgments [...]

**2** [...] and my insides came apart, and my bones were smashed to pieces [...]

**3** [...] and my heart spilled out like water, and my body melted like wax [...]

**4** [...] and my knees gave way like water running down a hillside [...]

**5** [...] and I cried out: Because of my sin I have been cut off [...]

**6** [...] from Your covenant. But then I remembered how powerful Your hand is [...]

**7** [...] along with how endlessly merciful You are, and I stood up and recovered [...]

**8** [...] and my spirit clung to its place, because I was leaning [...]

**9** [...] on Your faithful love, and on the depth of Your compassion [...]

**10** [...] because You wipe away sin, and You wash a person clean of guilt through Your goodness [...]

**11** [...] and [...] my strength [...] gave out before Your overwhelming glory [...]

**12** [...] and nothing was left, no strength [...] remained in me [...]

**13** [...] I was speechless, because what could I say that You do not already know [...]

**14** [...] and what could I announce that has not already been spoken? Everything [...]

**15** [...] is written down before You with the pen of eternal memory for every appointed moment [...]

**16** [...] across all eternity, and every cycle of the everlasting years [...]

**17** [...] each in their proper season, and none of it will be hidden [...]

**18** [...] from You. How can anyone account for their sin? [...]

**19** [...] and how can they make their case about their wrongdoing? [...]

**20** [...] and how can they respond when the verdict is just? [...]

**21** [...] Everything righteous belongs to You, God of all knowledge [...]

**22** [...] and all truthful counsel; but to us mortals belongs only the practice of wrongdoing [...]

**23** [...] and deceptive works. You created the very breath that powers the tongue [...]

**24** [...] and You know every word it will speak, and You designed what the lips produce [...]

**25** [...] before any of it existed. You laid out words on a blueprint [...]

**26** [...] and measured out every syllable of breath from the lips [...]

**27** [...] and You release sounds according to their hidden design [...]

**28** [...] and every outpouring of breath according to its calculation, so that all might know [...]

**29** [...] Your glory and tell of Your wonders [...]

**30** [...] but Your mercies [...] have been what kept me alive through all of this [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 25 is very fragmentary but contains some of the Hodayot's most viscerally physical poetry. The body-in-crisis sequence (heart pouring like water, flesh melting like wax, knees buckling) is rendered to preserve the immediate, embodied quality of the original. The divine-speech theology (25:23-28) — God as the creator of language itself — is a remarkable passage with implications for understanding Qumran's view of revelation.*
